knowledge:
- key_parameters: genome.size=An integer specifying the number of genes in the genomic background (the "universe"). This is a critical parameter as the significance of the overlap is highly sensitive to it ;; what=A character string in drawHeatmap (e.g., "Jaccard" or default "Odds Ratio") specifying which metric to visualize ;; ncolused=An integer specifying the number of colors to use in the heatmap ;; grid.col=A character string specifying the color palette for the heatmap grid (e.g., "Blues", "Oranges") ;; note.col=A character string specifying the color of the text notes (p-values) superimposed on the heatmap grids
- alternatives: Hypergeometric distribution (mathematically equivalent formulation of the contingency table solved by Fisher's exact test)
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have two or more gene lists (e.g., from ChIP-seq peak calling, RNA-seq expression groups, or pathway analyses) and want to statistically test and visualize whether their overlap is significant rather than occurring by chance.
- pitfalls: Modifying the slots of a GeneOverlap object (such as listA, listB, or genome.size) after creation will reset its status to untested, requiring you to call testGeneOverlap again ;; Underestimating or overestimating the genome.size (background universe) will drastically skew the resulting p-values, as a larger background size makes a given overlap size appear more statistically significant.

workflows.name: pairwise_gene_overlap
workflows.intent: Test the statistical significance of the overlap between two individual gene lists and retrieve detailed association statistics.
input: list1.txt (character vector of gene IDs for list A)
list2.txt (character vector of gene IDs for list B)
background_size (integer representing the total number of genes in the genomic background)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a GeneOverlap object using newGeneOverlap ;; 2. Run the statistical test using testGeneOverlap ;; 3. Print detailed results and retrieve specific statistics (intersection, odds ratio, contingency table, genome size) using accessors.
workflows.code:
go.obj <- newGeneOverlap(hESC.ChIPSeq.list$H3K4me3, 
                         hESC.RNASeq.list$"Exp High", 
                         genome.size=gs.RNASeq)
go.obj <- testGeneOverlap(go.obj)
print(go.obj)
head(getIntersection(go.obj))
getOddsRatio(go.obj)
getContbl(go.obj)
getGenomeSize(go.obj)

workflows.name: matrix_gene_overlap
workflows.intent: Compare multiple gene lists from two different gene sets in a pairwise matrix fashion, visualize the results as a heatmap, and extract specific comparison matrices.
input: set1.rds (named list of character vectors representing gene set A)
set2.rds (named list of character vectors representing gene set B)
background_size (integer representing the total number of genes in the genomic background)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a GeneOverlapMatrix object using newGOM ;; 2. Visualize the pairwise overlaps using drawHeatmap ;; 3. Extract matrices of p-values or odds ratios using getMatrix ;; 4. Retrieve overlapping gene lists for all comparisons using getNestedList ;; 5. Access individual pairwise GeneOverlap objects using matrix-like indexing.
workflows.code:
gom.obj <- newGOM(hESC.ChIPSeq.list, hESC.RNASeq.list, 
                  gs.RNASeq)
drawHeatmap(gom.obj)
getMatrix(gom.obj, name="pval")
getMatrix(gom.obj, "odds.ratio")
inter.nl <- getNestedList(gom.obj, name="intersection")
go.k4.high <- gom.obj[1, 1]
gom.obj["H3K9me3", "Exp Medium"]

workflows.name: self_comparison_overlap
workflows.intent: Perform a pairwise self-comparison of gene lists within a single gene set and visualize the results using customized heatmaps.
input: set1.rds (named list of character vectors representing a single gene set)
background_size (integer representing the total number of genes in the genomic background)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a GeneOverlapMatrix object for self-comparison using newGOM with a single gene set ;; 2. Visualize the upper triangular matrix using drawHeatmap ;; 3. Customize the heatmap colors, text colors, and plotted metrics (e.g., Jaccard index).
workflows.code:
gom.self <- newGOM(hESC.ChIPSeq.list, 
                   genome.size=gs.RNASeq)
drawHeatmap(gom.self)
drawHeatmap(gom.self, ncolused=5, grid.col="Blues", note.col="black")
drawHeatmap(gom.self, what="Jaccard", ncolused=3, grid.col="Oranges", 
            note.col="black")
